segments.text: For such a yogi, as such a Gyanam annam, differentiated perception is his food.
Differentated perception is his food.
He eats differentiated perception.
He digests differentiated perception in his own supreme nature of consciousness.
Yatpuram Gyanam Bandha He Tukhtam, previously, in first awakening of Srutra, in second Srutra,
you have already known that Gyanam Bandha, the bondage is differentiated knowledge.
Differentated perception is bondage.
That differentiated perception is directed by great yogis, great Shavite yogis in God consciousness.
When this differentiated perception is carried in God consciousness, that differentiated
perception does not live, then that differentiated perception expires.
So, there is no differentiated perception left behind.
It is why he has said here in Srutra, it is his food, that differentiated perception is
food because he takes it in, in his own God consciousness, Grecimanatta.
And digests it in his own supreme nature.
Yat Samvajitam Prohk, previously, this point is communicated in this Shloka.
Vikar Jatam Prithipatti Sathmiam, Ayakath, Minanath, Vitharka Jatam, Tadasa, Sarvam, Kavali,
Tadasa.
At that state, when he carries all this differentiated perception in one God consciousness and makes it
digest in that, then it is not only digestion of differentiated perception, along with differentiated
perception, death is digested, Kalam, time is digested, Kalapalapam, all actions good or bad
are digested.
Vikar Jatam, all changes of life are digested.
Prithipatti Sathmiam, all perceptions good or bad are digested.
And all discussions on the point of Adhaita, monastic discussions are, dualistic discussions
are digested in that supreme oneness of God consciousness, when that differentiated perception
is being digested or is being carried in the kingdom of God consciousness.
This is one way of explaining this sutra.
This second way of explaining this sutra is as follows.
Atajaya atsorupu yamarsha atma-kham jnanam, or take jnan as supreme one, not differentiated
perception, knowledge of your own nature, knowledge of your own real self, that is jnan.
Jat sorupu yamarsha atma-kham jnanam, tath asya-nam, that is his food.
That knowledge is his food, for sathayogi, which knowledge?
Real knowledge of self is his food.
In one way he has explained the differentiated knowledge is his food.
All kinds of differentiated perceptions are his food because he carries them in from
differentiatedness to undifferentiatedness.
He carries them from darkness to light, he carries them from sadness to joy.
So everything for him is joyous, everything is full of light, everything is filled with
glory for him.
This is the one way of explaining jnan.
The other way of explaining jnan is real jnan, real knowledge of your own nature, is his
food because he gets satisfied with it.
He is always satisfied with it, he doesn't care for physical food, he doesn't mind for physical
food.
Of course he eats, he does not starve, but he does not mind, he is always intoxicated in
his own self.
Because purna paritrafthi kaerita ya saathmikshranti he tu, because it gives him entire satisfaction.
That knowledge of real nature gives him entire satisfaction.
It is said in vijñana bairava also.
Atraya ktam yuktis te yot padeyat dina dinam bharita kaerita saatra triftir atyanda purnata.
In this world of means, in this world of upayas, in this world of 112 ways of entering in
supreme nature.
In vijñana bairava you already know there are 112 ways to enter by which you get entry
in God consciousness, from individual consciousness, you enter in God consciousness.
There are 112 ways explained in vijñana bairava.
This is the quotation from vijñana bairava tantra.
He says atra ektam yuktis te.
No matter what way is there, anyway, take one way from 112 ways, suggest only one way from
112 ways.
By meditating on that state, meditating on that way, yā bairita kaerita dina dhenam utpadeyat
the fullness that he experiences day by day, by maintaining meditative mood on that one
way, saatra triftir atyanda purnata.
That gives him perfect satisfaction and perfect fullness of self.
Yuktiri atra dādhśotāra shatbhumyaka ghanaru paiwar yuktiri, the means, the way, the way here
is, here you should know dādhśotāra shatbhumyaka, one way from 112 ways, anyway, from 112
ways.
This is narrated in spanda, in this loka, Prabhupada sarvada tishti, always maintained awareness
in each and every action of your life.
If you miss that awareness, you are gone, you have finished that reality of life.
So you must be aware, the more you are aware of thoughts, no thought will come in you.
If you are aware of your thoughts, what thoughts you have in your mind, no thought will be
seen there.
If you are fully aware, not on sidelines, you should not be established awareness on sidelines,
be full aware of what you are thinking, you won't think anything.
If you are aware of what is happening next, nothing will happen.
If you are aware that you are dying, you won't die.
If you are aware, you are going from wakefulness to dreaming state, you won't go.
On the contrary, you will get entry in God consciousness by establishing this awareness.
This is the greatness of awareness.
He has to be aware of what he is thinking.
If you are aware always in continuation, you are aware, you won't think anything, you are
one-pointed, you reside in one-pointed state of God consciousness.
If you are unaware, if you miss that awareness, you miss the reality of life, not everything.
Everything used to be missed, you miss the reality of your life.
When this yogi does not maintain awareness in continuity, this state, you must remain,
Prabhupada means aware, fully aware, Prabhupada, Sarvada in continuation, in continuity, always,
you must remain aware of what you are doing, what you are talking, you won't talk rubbish
things there.
If you are aware of what you are talking, if you are aware of what you are speaking, you
would speak lies, if you are aware of what you are doing, you won't do that.
This is the greatness of awareness, that makes you, that makes you filled with that great
God consciousness.
When this way, one does not maintain awareness in continuity, sata, sata means in continuity.
Then although he possesses knowledge of God consciousness, I say, Audhaanat, Avalepa,
many likes awareness at many, many points, many, many, many points he passes through many
points, many avenues, many corners, many corners, many, diversions, where he likes awareness.
For instance, if you are aware of God consciousness, now, after a while, you are unaware.
You are missing that awareness.
After a while, you are again maintaining that awareness.
This is not the way to maintain awareness, awareness should be maintained in continuity.
When in continuity, you don't maintain awareness, then Audhaanat, Avalepa, awareness is missing
at many points.
